skill.name: contract-helper
skill.description: Draft and review influencer agreements covering deliverables, compensation, usage rights, exclusivity, approvals, disclosures, termination, and negotiation points.
skill.summary: Build practical influencer agreements and review contract terms for missing clauses, red flags, and negotiation opportunities.
skill.author: aaron-he-zhu

security_audit.summary: All 36 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown syntax, relative documentation links, metadata URLs, and ordinary marketing language. No executable shell code, network request, reconnaissance, or arbitrary path traversal is present. The skill does create a medium-severity privacy risk by persisting confidential contract terms without an explicit consent or retention check.

remediation.issue: Contract drafts and signed commercial terms are written to persistent memory and an events log.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before persistence, minimize stored fields, exclude payment details, and document retention and access controls.

remediation.issue: The output filename includes a topic value derived from the request.
remediation.suggestion: Convert the topic to a safe slug and verify the resolved path remains inside the designated contract-helper directory.

content.value_statement: Influencer deals often leave payment, usage, and approval terms unclear. This skill drafts structured agreements and reviews existing terms for risks and omissions.
actual_capabilities: Collects parties, deliverables, compensation, platforms, dates, usage rights, exclusivity, and approval requirements.
Drafts an eleven-section influencer partnership agreement with signatures.
Reviews incoming terms for missing provisions and common contract red flags.
Explains material clauses, their purpose, and concerns to examine.
Creates negotiation guidance for usage rights, exclusivity, revisions, approvals, and payment timing.
limitations: Provides general templates and guidance, not legal advice.
Does not confirm enforceability under a specific jurisdiction.
Does not negotiate outreach terms before the parties agree in principle.
Requires legal counsel review before execution, especially for significant partnerships.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Brand Agreement
use_cases.description: Turn an approved campaign scope into a complete creator agreement with clear deliverables, payment, rights, and deadlines.

use_cases.title: Review Agency Terms
use_cases.description: Check incoming agency paper for broad licenses, excessive exclusivity, unlimited revisions, weak payment terms, and missing protections.

use_cases.title: Standardize Contract Templates
use_cases.description: Create a reusable agreement framework that legal teams can adapt for different campaign sizes and platforms.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Simple Agreement
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft an influencer agreement for [deliverables] on [platform] for [payment], including dates, basic usage rights, and FTC disclosure.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs a clear agreement for a small campaign.

prompt_templates.title: Review Existing Terms
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these influencer contract terms. List missing provisions, red flags, questions, and suggested changes: [paste terms].
prompt_templates.scenario: A creator receives contract terms from a brand or agency.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Reusable Template
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a reusable creator partnership template for [company], covering deliverables, compensation, licensing, exclusivity, approvals, compliance, termination, and signatures.
prompt_templates.scenario: A marketing team wants consistent agreements across campaigns.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Negotiation Positions
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [brand proposal] with [creator proposal]. Recommend balanced language for usage, whitelisting, exclusivity, revisions, payment, cancellation, and dispute resolution.
prompt_templates.scenario: An experienced manager needs clause-level negotiation guidance.

output_examples.input: Draft an agreement for two Instagram posts at $500.
output: Scope: Two Instagram posts following the approved brief.
Payment: $250 at signing and $250 after publication.
Rights: Non-exclusive use on owned channels for twelve months.
Compliance: Each post must include a clear sponsorship disclosure.

output_examples.input: Review a contract requesting perpetual worldwide rights and unlimited revisions.
output: High concern: The perpetual worldwide license is broader than the campaign requires.
High concern: Unlimited revisions create unbounded work.
Suggested position: Limit rights by channel and duration, and include two revision rounds.

best_practices: Provide exact deliverables, dates, fees, platforms, and rights before requesting a draft.
Mark unresolved terms as TBD and assign an owner and deadline.
Ask qualified counsel to review the final agreement before execution.
anti_patterns: Do not accept perpetual usage rights without considering scope and compensation.
Do not leave approval standards, revision limits, or payment triggers subjective.
Do not treat generated contract language as jurisdiction-specific legal advice.

faq.question: Does this skill provide legal advice?
faq.answer: No. It provides general contract guidance and templates that require review by qualified legal counsel.

faq.question: Can it review an agency contract?
faq.answer: Yes. Paste the terms, and it can identify omissions, red flags, questions, and negotiation points.

faq.question: Which clauses does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers scope, payment, licensing, exclusivity, approvals, disclosures, warranties, confidentiality, indemnification, termination, disputes, and signatures.

faq.question: Can it create a short agreement?
faq.answer: Yes. It can remove complex sections when they do not fit the campaign size or risk.

faq.question: Does it support FTC disclosure terms?
faq.answer: Yes. The template includes sponsorship disclosures and platform compliance requirements.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the parties, campaign, deliverables, dates, compensation, platforms, usage rights, exclusivity, approvals, and any existing terms.
